clue.text: With which one can do as one likes

definitions.text: With which one can do as one likes

parts.words: With which one can do as one likes
parts.note: a riddling description of the liberty to behave however you please, the whole clue read as a definition

explanation.surface: A question about what lets a person please themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberty to choose your own conduct is exactly what lets someone behave as they wish.

clue.text: One's last place of education?

parts.note: the question mark invites reading 'last' literally: the establishment where schooling is completed, rather than the old girls' academy for social polish

explanation.surface: A question about where someone's schooling ended.
explanation.definitionFit: A private college where young women were polished for society was traditionally the final stage of their education.

clue.text: Queen right or wrong in this?

parts.note: ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Asking whether the monarch is right or wrong about something.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the phrase 'in error': if you are in this state, you are wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a mistake means being wrong, so 'wrong in this' describes a mistake.

clue.text: Pull clear ofthe trap

parts.note: to drag is to pull along
net means clear after deductions, as in net profit

explanation.surface: Pulling something free of a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear' looks like a verb (free from), but it is the adjective, as in a clear or net profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishing or police net that sweeps everything up serves as a trap.

clue.text: Mother upset Denis and the girls

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of the name are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Mum has upset Denis and the girls in the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges DENIS to IDENS, which follows MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidens are young unmarried women, an old word for girls.

clue.text: More whimsical pigeon connoisseur

definitions.meaning: comparative of the adjective meaning capricious or ornate
someone who breeds and judges birds such as pigeons as a hobby

explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of fanciful-sounding 'fancy' means more whimsical, and a breeder of show pigeons is known as a pigeon enthusiast or keeper of that name.

clue.text: Happened to have taken risks

definitions.meaning: to do something by accident, as in 'I happened to see him'
to gamble or risk it, as in 'they risked it'

explanation.definitionFit: The verb meaning occur by luck covers 'happened to', and 'risked it' covers having taken a gamble.

clue.text: There is no distinction between such items

definitions.text: There is no distinction between such items

parts.words: There is no distinction between such items
parts.note: describes things alike in every respect, so that nothing tells them apart

explanation.surface: An observation that some objects cannot be told apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Things exactly alike in every detail have nothing to distinguish one from another.

clue.text: There is no reason behind such a driving impulse

definitions.text: There is no reason behind such a driving impulse

parts.words: There is no reason behind such a driving impulse
parts.note: describes an inborn urge that acts without thought or reasoning

explanation.surface: A remark about an urge that has no rational cause.
explanation.definitionFit: An innate urge works without conscious reasoning, prompting action by inborn drive.

clue.text: Story of arrival in the country

indicators.note: in places the short form for arrival inside the word for a country

parts.note: a nation is a country
ARR is the timetable abbreviation for arrival

explanation.surface: A tale of someone arriving in a land.
explanation.definitionFit: A telling or recounting of events is a story.

clue.text: One man to act on behalf of another

definitions.text: to act on behalf of another

parts.note: a means one
a gent is a gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: Describing a representative who acts for someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads with 'One man' as the subject: someone to act for another person.
explanation.definitionFit: A representative acting for another person, like a literary or estate representative.

clue.text: Unusual way to set in rows

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
to range things is to arrange them in rows or lines

explanation.surface: An odd method of arranging things in lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Something odd or out of the ordinary is unusual.

clue.text: To put it in a nicer fashion, he urges one on

indicators.note: put it in tells us to place the little word inside the other letters
put it in tells us to place the little word inside the other letters
to fashion is to shape, so the letters of nicer are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A euphemism for a man who eggs people on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' rearranges NICER to INCER, and 'put it in' places IT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: One who provokes or stirs others to act is someone urging them on.

clue.text: Word from one not in agreement North ofthe Border

definitions.text: Word from one not in agreement North ofthe Border

parts.words: Word from one not in agreement North ofthe Border
parts.note: a dissenting word in Scots dialect: what someone in Scotland says for no

explanation.surface: What a disagreeing Scot would say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North of the Border' means in Scotland, seen from England.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect the negative reply is spelt this way, the Scottish no.

clue.text: Little devil mixes suet using force

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil

indicators.note: mixes means stirs the letters of suet together into a new order

explanation.surface: A mischievous child forcefully mixing suet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixes' turns SUET into ETUS, after IMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentum or driving force is impetus.

clue.text: Jingoistic Irishman at S. American city with a twitch

parts.note: Pat, short for Patrick, is the stock Irishman in crosswords
Rio de Janeiro in Brazil
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A flag-waving Irishman in Rio with a nervous twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Jingoism is extreme, aggressive love of country.

clue.text: One in France with a girl

parts.note: un is French for one

explanation.surface: Someone in France with a girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Una is a girl's name.

clue.text: Root said to be far-reaching

definitions.meaning: relating to the root, as in a mathematical or word root

explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from Latin for root, and in politics it means sweeping or thorough-going.

clue.text: Has to remove the remains

indicators.note: to remove is read as to re-move, shifting the three letters into another order

explanation.surface: Someone must clear away the leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left after a fire, or a cremation, is the powdery residue.

clue.text: Name-tag redesigned by security employee

indicators.note: redesigned means the letters of the badge are laid out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A guard's identity badge has been given a new look.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatekeeper guards an entrance, a security job.

clue.text: Famous Italian from Minorca!

indicators.note: from here signals that the name is made out of the island's letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrated Italian who comes from a Spanish island.
explanation.walkthrough: Guglielmo Marconi was the Italian radio pioneer; his name is an exact rearrangement of MINORCA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian inventor of wireless telegraphy is a famous Italian.

clue.text: Checking growth by pinching

definitions.meaning: as in 'nipped in the bud', halting development
squeezing sharply between finger and thumb

explanation.definitionFit: To stop something developing early is to cut it off at the bud, and a sharp squeeze is a pinch.

clue.text: Charlie takes article from padre

indicators.note: takes ... from means the article is removed from the clergyman's title

parts.note: a padre is a chaplain, a military clergyman
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Charlie removes an item from the clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' joins the deletion: A is taken from CHAPLAIN. Charlie Chaplin was the silent-film comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie is the first name of the famous silent-screen comic.

clue.text: Cover Stanley put on a revolving cylinder

indicators.note: in a down clue, put on means the first piece is placed on top of the second

parts.note: a cap is a cover or lid
Stan is short for Stanley

explanation.surface: A man named Stanley puts a lid on a rotating drum.
explanation.definitionFit: On ships, a vertical revolving drum used for winding cable is this.

clue.text: Give instructions to settle

definitions.meaning: to make arrangements or plans, directing how something is done
to agree or fix, as in fixing a date

explanation.definitionFit: Organising matters means giving directions, and fixing terms is settling them.

clue.text: I had taken a girl

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Confessing to having taken a girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Ida is a girl's name.

clue.text: Expression of encouragement heard to come from a bird

definitions.meaning: a clicking sound made to urge on a horse or baby

definitions.text: heard to come from a bird
definitions.meaning: a chirping call such as a sparrow makes

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a twittering birdsong and a clicking noise used to cheer on or encourage.

clue.text: Have a drink before ten perhaps — that's a bad sign

indicators.note: before places the drink in front of the jumbled number

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the number's letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Drinking port before ten in the morning bodes ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges TEN to ENT, after PORT; 'Have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen of something ominous is a bad sign.

clue.text: Those chosen from the literati

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A select group chosen from the intelligentsia.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took only 'Those' as definition with 'chosen from' as indicator; but 'Those chosen' is the definition (the elite are the chosen few), leaving 'from' as the hiding signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The select few, picked as the best, form the cream of society.

clue.text: Without doubt some will excel

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Certainly some people are going to do brilliantly.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass someone is to excel them, beat them.

clue.text: Under canvas perhaps I go on purpose

parts.note: camping, one is in a tent, under canvas
taken as written

explanation.surface: Perhaps I'm off camping deliberately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' notes camping is one example of being under canvas; 'go' is a link placing I and ON after it. 'Under canvas' is a British idiom for sleeping in a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim or plan is one's purpose.

clue.text: Having no attraction-like un investments?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Having no attraction-like un investments?' is garbled by OCR ('-like un') and no scan or search gives the printed wording, so the second reading cannot be quoted.
